It gives si_dimension = L and dimension_vector = [0,1,0,0,0,0,0], which supports the candidate assignment k_rms as a length (L=1) and all other exponents zero, matching the before_si_exponents.

The record pq_height_kurtosis provides the canonical definition for surface-height kurtosis (symbol Ku) as the 'Fourth standardized moment of the surface-height distribution.' Standardized moments are dimensionless; the entry lists si_dimension = 1 and dimension_vector = [0,0,0,0,0,0,0], which matches the candidate before_si_exponents for Ku (all zeros).

The record pq_effective_surface_slope defines effective surface slope (symbols: ES, E_x) as the 'Mean absolute gradient of surface height in a specified horizontal direction.' As a derivative of height with respect to horizontal distance this ratio is dimensionless; the entry gives si_dimension = 1 and dimension_vector = [0,0,0,0,0,0,0], supporting ES having all zero base exponents as in the candidate before_si_exponents.

The record pq_porosity provides the canonical definition for porosity (symbols Po, P_o, phi_p) as a 'Fraction of void or open volume/area' and lists si_dimension = 1 with dimension_vector = [0,0,0,0,0,0,0]. candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: ks (equivalent sand-grain roughness) has dimensions of length; Ra is a length, so the ratio ks/Ra is dimensionless. Therefore the target dimensionless ratio can be expressed as a function of the dimensionless statistical descriptors (Sk, Ku, ES, Po) and any non-dimensional combinations of the length-based roughness scales (Ra, kt, k_rms) that cancel to yield a pure number. Empirically, one expects ks/Ra = f(kt/Ra, k_rms/Ra, Sk, Ku, ES, Po), but the primary point is ks/Ra is itself dimensionless.

variables.physical_definition: First-order absolute moment (arithmetic mean of absolute deviations) of surface height fluctuations
Peak-to-valley height (difference between highest peak and lowest valley of the surface profile)
Root-mean-square height of surface roughness (square root of the mean squared height deviations)
Skewness of height fluctuations (third central moment divided by the cube of the rms height) — dimensionless
Kurtosis of height fluctuations (fourth standardized moment) — dimensionless
Effective streamwise slope of the roughness (mean slope in the flow direction) — dimensionless
Surface porosity (fraction of surface area that is void) — dimensionless

Problem:
Perform dimensional analysis for sand-grain roughness parameterization to derive the dimensionless relationship governing the normalized equivalent sand-grain roughness (denoted as ks/Ra).
This analysis uses ONLY the following 7 physical quantities as input parameters:
the first-order absolute moment of height fluctuations, Ra;
the peak-to-valley height, kt;
the root-mean-square height, k_rms;
the third central moment of roughness height fluctuations divided by the cube of their root-mean-square height, Sk;
the kurtosis of roughness height fluctuations, Ku;
the effective streamwise slope of the roughness, ES;
the surface porosity, Po.

final_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: ks (equivalent sand-grain roughness) has dimensions of length; Ra is a length, so the ratio ks/Ra is dimensionless. Therefore the target dimensionless ratio can be expressed as a function of the dimensionless statistical descriptors (Sk, Ku, ES, Po) and any non-dimensional combinations of the length-based roughness scales (Ra, kt, k_rms) that cancel to yield a pure number. Empirically, one expects ks/Ra = f(kt/Ra, k_rms/Ra, Sk, Ku, ES, Po), but the primary point is ks/Ra is itself dimensionless.

variables.physical_definition: First-order absolute moment (arithmetic mean of absolute deviations) of surface height fluctuations
Peak-to-valley height (difference between highest peak and lowest valley of the surface profile)
Root-mean-square height of surface roughness (square root of the mean squared height deviations)
Skewness of height fluctuations (third central moment divided by the cube of the rms height) — dimensionless
Kurtosis of height fluctuations (fourth standardized moment) — dimensionless
Effective streamwise slope of the roughness (mean slope in the flow direction) — dimensionless
Surface porosity (fraction of surface area that is void) — dimensionless
